title: Quasi-compact open immersions of algebraic spaces are finitely presented
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme, and quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. A morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback along every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source, and quasi-separated if its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. An affine morphism is representable by schemes and has affine scheme source after every affine scheme test. Local finite type and local finite presentation are tested on compatible etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation. An open immersion is a representable morphism that is an open immersion on every scheme test [def-a1-space-open-subspace]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact open immersion of algebraic spaces. Then $j$ is of finite presentation. No quasi-compactness, separation or Noetherian hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06CN (lemma-open-immersion-locally-finite-presentation); quasi-separatedness follows from the identity diagonal of an open immersion

proof.text: Choose a scheme atlas $p:V\to X$, representable surjective etale, by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Set $W=V\times_XU$. By [def-a1-space-open-subspace], $W$ is a scheme and $j_V:W\to V$ identifies it with an open subscheme of $V$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $W\to U$ is representable surjective etale. Consequently $W\to V$ is a compatible scheme-chart presentation of $j$, so local finite presentation of this scheme map proves local finite presentation of $j$, by the chart convention in the statement.

source.place: Tag 06CN (lemma-open-immersion-locally-finite-presentation), reduction to scheme tests; spaces.tex Tag 02YO (lemma-representable-transformations-property-implication)

proof.text: Fix $w\in W$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] in $V$ to its open subset $j_V(W)$: there is an affine open $D=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq j_V(W)$ containing $j_V(w)$. By [def-weil-open-immersion], $j_V^{-1}(D)\to D$ is an isomorphism of open subschemes. In these affine coordinates its ring map is $A\to A$, which is a finite presentation with zero generators and zero relations. Thus the affine neighbourhoods $j_V^{-1}(D)$ and $D$ satisfy [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] at $w$. Every point has such neighbourhoods, so $j_V$, and hence $j$, is locally of finite presentation. This writes out the local-isomorphism argument; it invokes no finiteness hypothesis on $V$ or $X$.

source.place: Tag 01TT (lemma-open-immersion-locally-finite-presentation), proof: an open immersion is a local isomorphism

proof.text: For any $S$-scheme $T$ and $a,b\in U(T)$ with $j(a)=j(b)=c$, both give sections of the scheme projection $T\times_XU\to T$. This projection is an open immersion by [def-a1-space-open-subspace]. It identifies its source with an open subscheme of $T$ by [def-weil-open-immersion], so it has at most one section: a section forces that open subset to be all of $T$, and is the inverse of the resulting isomorphism. Hence $a=b$. The diagonal $\Delta_j:U\to U\times_XU$ is therefore an isomorphism: on every test $T$ its inverse sends $(a,b)$ with $j(a)=j(b)$ to $a=b$; the inverse and diagonal commute with restriction maps. The sheaf fibre product here is the fibre product of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

source.place: Tag 01L7 (lemma-immersions-monomorphisms), open-immersion argument, written on sheaf sections

proof.text: For every affine scheme $T\to U\times_XU$, the pullback of the isomorphism $\Delta_j$ is isomorphic to $T$. The scheme $T$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Its identity atlas is surjective etale, so it is also quasi-compact with the space convention of the statement. Thus every affine test of $\Delta_j$ has quasi-compact source: $\Delta_j$ is quasi-compact and $j$ is quasi-separated. Together with local finite presentation from step 2 and the given quasi-compactness of $j$, these are exactly the three conditions defining finite presentation in the statement. The same arguments apply when $U$ is empty, with the pointwise assertion of step 2 vacuous.

source.place: Tag 06CN, together with definition-finite-presentation; diagonal argument as in morphisms.tex Tag 01TU (lemma-quasi-compact-open-immersion-finite-presentation)
